key_insight: MediX-R1 enables medical multimodal LLMs to produce clinically grounded, free-form answers by fine-tuning a vision-language backbone with Group-Based Reinforcement Learning and a composite reward that enforces strict clinical correctness while allowing paraphrases.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of training and evaluation methods that produce and validate open-ended, clinically accurate multimodal answers instead of limited multiple-choice outputs.
method: Fine-tune a vision-language backbone using Group-Based Reinforcement Learning to handle diverse clinical data and training cohorts.
Optimize with a composite reward: (a) an LLM-based binary accuracy judge (YES/NO) for strict semantic correctness and (b) a medical embedding-based semantic reward to accept valid paraphrases.
Target open-ended free-text responses rather than constrained multiple-choice formats to improve clinical reasoning and expressivity.
impact: Provides a practical training and evaluation recipe for building safer, more useful medical MLLMs that deliver reliable free-text clinical answers—improving downstream usability for diagnostics, reporting, and decision support.

paper_title: MediX-R1: Open Ended Medical Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Sahal Shaji Mullappilly, Mohammed Irfan Kurpath, Omair Mohamed, Mohamed Zidan, Fahad Khan
